title: Module cohomology preserves multiplication by a global section
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $r\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and $\tau:G\to G$ an endomorphism such that $\tau_U(t)=r|_U\,t$ for every open $U$ and section $t\in G(U)$. For every $q\ge0$ and $x\in H^q(X,G)$, with module cohomology defined by [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], $H^q(X,\tau)(x)=r x$.

source.place: Tag 01DZ, section-cohomology-sheaves, equation-cohomology-modules: module cohomology computed by injective resolutions

proof.text: Define the scalar endomorphism on each sheaf by restriction of r to every open. Naturality of restrictions and linearity of sheaf morphisms imply that it commutes with every module-sheaf morphism. The section formula identifies tau with this endomorphism.

Use enough injectives to choose an injective resolution I of G. The scalar endomorphisms in each degree define a chain map phi since they commute with the differentials, and extend tau. Mathlib InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality computes the derived map via phi.

Evaluation at the top open takes each component of phi to r times the identity. On the short complex computing degree q, phi is r times the identity. Mathlib ShortComplex.homologyMap_smul and homologyMap_id therefore compute its homology map as r times the identity. The resolution comparison is a module isomorphism, so cancel its injective hom map and use linearity to conclude.
